Power analysis for exploratory factor analysis

Source: R/efa_power.R
efa_power.Rd

Analyses power for exploratory factor analysis in one of two modes, chosen with mode.

mode = "rmsea" (the default) gives the analytic power of the root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA) tests of close and not-close fit (MacCallum, Browne, & Sugawara, 1996). Give a sample size to get the power of the test, or give a target power to get the necessary sample size.

mode = "simulation" runs a Monte-Carlo study: it draws n_datasets samples from a known population (with efa_simulate()), analyses each sample, and reports how frequently the analysis finds the population structure. A call with Lambda or R and no mode uses this mode.

Usage

efa_power(
  mode = c("rmsea", "simulation"),
  type = c("close", "notclose"),
  eps0 = NULL,
  eps1 = NULL,
  N = NULL,
  n_vars = NULL,
  n_factors = NULL,
  df = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  power = NULL,
  group = 1,
  Lambda = NULL,
  Phi = NULL,
  Psi = NULL,
  R = NULL,
  n_datasets = 500,
  criteria = c("EKC", "MAP"),
  estimator = "PAF",
  rotation = "oblimin",
  recovery_threshold = 0.95,
  model_error = c("TKL", "CB", "WB", "none"),
  target_rmsea = NULL,
  target_cfi = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  p = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  k = lifecycle::deprecated()
)

Arguments

mode

character. "rmsea" (the default) or "simulation". If mode is not given, Lambda or R selects "simulation". type, eps0, eps1, df, alpha, power, and group apply only to RMSEA mode. The arguments marked Simulation mode apply only to simulation mode. An argument of the other mode is an error.

type

character. The RMSEA test: "close" or "notclose". See Details.

eps0

numeric. The null-hypothesis RMSEA. Default is 0.05.

eps1

numeric. The alternative-hypothesis RMSEA, at which power is calculated. Default is 0.08 for type = "close" and 0.01 for type = "notclose".

N

numeric. The sample size. In RMSEA mode, the total of all groups: give N to get the power, or leave it NULL to get the required N. In simulation mode (required), the size of each sample.

n_vars

numeric. The number of variables. In RMSEA mode, it gives df together with n_factors. In simulation mode, it comes from the population; if given, it must agree.

n_factors

numeric. The number of factors. In RMSEA mode, it gives df together with n_vars. In simulation mode, the true number of factors: necessary with R; with Lambda, if given, it must agree with ncol(Lambda).

df

numeric. The model degrees of freedom. Give df, or n_vars and n_factors, which give df = group * ((n_vars - n_factors)^2 - (n_vars + n_factors)) / 2 (a separate EFA in each group).

alpha

numeric. The significance level. Default is 0.05.

power

numeric. The target power for the required N. Default is NULL, which uses 0.80 if N is also NULL. Give only one of N and power.

group

numeric. The number of groups of equal size. Default is 1. See Details.

Lambda

matrix. Simulation mode. The population loadings (variables by factors) of a factor-model population. Structure recovery is available only with Lambda.

Phi

matrix. Simulation mode. The population factor correlations. Only used with Lambda. Default is orthogonal factors.

Psi

numeric or matrix. Simulation mode. The population unique variances. Only used with Lambda. See efa_simulate().

R

matrix. Simulation mode. A population correlation matrix, instead of Lambda. It needs n_factors.

n_datasets

numeric. Simulation mode. The number of samples. Default is 500.

criteria

character. Simulation mode. The retention criteria for the hit-rate: any of "CD", "EKC", "HULL", "KGC", "MAP", "NEST", "PARALLEL", and "SMT" (see efa_retain()). Default is c("EKC", "MAP"). The criteria use the efa_retain() defaults and estimator. "CD" and "HULL" are much slower.

estimator

character. Simulation mode. The estimator of the recovery fit and the retention criteria: "PAF" (the default), "ML", or "ULS".

rotation

character. Simulation mode. The rotation of the recovery fit (see efa_fit()). Default is "oblimin", as in efa_fit(). Recovery only reorders and reflects the factors. Thus, "none" with more than one factor understates recovery.

recovery_threshold

numeric. Simulation mode. The Tucker congruence that a replicate must reach to be recovered. Default is 0.95, at which Lorenzo-Seva and ten Berge (2006) consider two factors equal.

model_error

character. Simulation mode. The efa_simulate() method for model error: "TKL" (the default; it adds minor common factors), "CB", "WB", or "none". It applies only with target_rmsea or target_cfi, which need Lambda. Note that efa_simulate() has the default "CB".

target_rmsea

numeric. Simulation mode. The population RMSEA. Default is NULL (no model error). See efa_simulate().

target_cfi

numeric. Simulation mode. The population CFI (only with "TKL"). Default is NULL. See efa_simulate().

seed

numeric. Simulation mode. An optional seed for a reproducible result. Default is NULL.

p, k

Use n_vars and n_factors.

Value

An object of class efa_power. For mode = "rmsea", a list with:

power

The power at N (for a required N, at least the target power).

N

The total sample size: the given N, or the required N (a multiple of group).

N_per_group

The group size N / group.

crit

The critical chi-square value.

ncp

The noncentrality parameters under the null (H0) and the alternative (H1).

solve_for

"power" or "N": the calculated quantity.

settings

The inputs: mode, type, eps0, eps1, df, n_vars, n_factors, alpha, group, and the target power (NULL if solve_for is "power").

For mode = "simulation", a list with:

hit_rate

The hit-rate per criterion, and per variant if a criterion has more than one.

hits

A data frame with one row per criterion or variant: criterion, the number of replicates with a suggestion (n_valid), the number of hits (hits), hit_rate (hits / n_datasets), and its Monte Carlo standard error (mcse).

recovery

For Lambda, a list with the recovery rates (min_rate, mean_rate), the threshold, and the number of replicates with a congruence (n_valid); NULL for R. Non-converged and Heywood solutions are included.

convergence

A list with n_datasets, the number of completed fits (n_fit_ok), the number of those that converged (n_converged) or have a Heywood case (n_heywood), and the rates fit_rate (of all datasets), convergence_rate, and heywood_rate (of the completed fits).

replicates

The per-replicate values: the suggested numbers of factors (n_hat), the matched congruences (rec_min, rec_mean), the flags converged, heywood, and fit_ok, and fit_error, the error message of a failed fit (NA otherwise).

k_true

The true number of factors.

model_error

The efa_simulate() model-error record, or NULL.

settings

The simulation inputs.

RMSEA mode

Power increases with the sample size, the degrees of freedom, and the difference between the null and the alternative RMSEA (MacCallum et al., 1996). type selects the test:

"close"

The null hypothesis is close fit (RMSEA \(\le\) eps0, conventionally 0.05). Power is the probability to reject it if the RMSEA is eps1 (conventionally 0.08). eps0 must be smaller than eps1.

"notclose"

The null hypothesis is not-close fit (RMSEA \(\ge\) eps0). Power is the probability to reject it if the RMSEA is eps1 (conventionally 0.01). eps0 must be larger than eps1.

The required sample size is the smallest N that reaches power. The result applies to the RMSEA test only: it does not make sure that the estimates are precise. With many degrees of freedom, the required N can be smaller than the number of variables. The sample correlation matrix is then singular (MacCallum et al., 1996, p. 144). If n_vars is known, such a sample size gives a warning.

With group > 1, N is the total of group groups of equal size, and df is that of the whole multiple-group model. The noncentrality parameter is \((N - G)\, df\, \varepsilon^2 / G\) for \(G\) groups (Steiger, 1998). Thus, at a given df, power depends only on the group size N / group, and a required N is group times the smallest group size that reaches power.

Simulation mode

efa_simulate() draws n_datasets samples of size N from the population. The true number of factors, k_true, is ncol(Lambda), or n_factors for a correlation matrix R. Without target_rmsea or target_cfi, a factor-model population fits the model exactly, which gives optimistic results. A misfit target makes the population more realistic (MacCallum, 2003).

The hit-rate and the recovery rates are proportions of all n_datasets replicates:

Hit-rate

A criterion in criteria suggests k_true factors. A replicate where the criterion fails or gives no suggestion counts as a miss.

Structure recovery (factor-model populations only)

The k_true-factor model is fitted with efa_fit(), and its factors are matched to the population loadings. A replicate is recovered if the smallest (min) or the mean (mean) Tucker congruence of the matched factors reaches recovery_threshold (Lorenzo-Seva & ten Berge, 2006). A failed fit counts as not recovered.

The Monte Carlo standard error of a rate \(p\) is \(\sqrt{p(1 - p) / n}\) for \(n\) replicates (Morris, White, & Crowther, 2019). The convergence and Heywood rates are proportions of the fits that completed. If fits fail, a warning gives their number and the first cause.

The replicates are analysed in parallel with future.apply; set a parallel plan with future::plan(). With a fixed seed, the result does not depend on the number of workers, and your random-number stream does not change.

References

Lorenzo-Seva, U., & ten Berge, J. M. F. (2006). Tucker's congruence coefficient as a meaningful index of factor similarity. Methodology, 2(2), 57-64. doi:10.1027/1614-2241.2.2.57

MacCallum, R. C. (2003). 2001 Presidential Address: Working with imperfect models. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 38(1), 113-139. doi:10.1207/S15327906MBR3801_5

MacCallum, R. C., Browne, M. W., & Sugawara, H. M. (1996). Power analysis and determination of sample size for covariance structure modeling. Psychological Methods, 1(2), 130-149. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.1.2.130

Morris, T. P., White, I. R., & Crowther, M. J. (2019). Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods. Statistics in Medicine, 38(11), 2074-2102. doi:10.1002/sim.8086

Steiger, J. H. (1998). A note on multiple sample extensions of the RMSEA fit index. Structural Equation Modeling, 5(4), 411-419. doi:10.1080/10705519809540115

See also

efa_simulate() draws the samples of simulation mode. efa_retain() implements the retention criteria.

Other power analysis: plot.efa_power(), print.efa_power()

Examples

# Power of the test of close fit at N = 200 for a 100-df model
efa_power(df = 100, N = 200)
#> 
#> ── RMSEA power analysis ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> Test of close fit: H0 RMSEA ≤ .050 vs. H1 RMSEA = .080.
#> alpha = .050 · df = 100
#> 
#> Power = .955 at N = 200.

# df from the number of variables and factors
efa_power(n_vars = 20, n_factors = 3, N = 200)
#> 
#> ── RMSEA power analysis ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> Test of close fit: H0 RMSEA ≤ .050 vs. H1 RMSEA = .080.
#> alpha = .050 · df = 133
#> 
#> Power = .986 at N = 200.

# Required sample size for 80% power
efa_power(df = 100, power = 0.80)
#> 
#> ── RMSEA power analysis ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> Test of close fit: H0 RMSEA ≤ .050 vs. H1 RMSEA = .080.
#> alpha = .050 · df = 100
#> 
#> Required N = 132 for a power of .800 (achieved .802).

# Test of not-close fit
efa_power(df = 100, N = 200, type = "notclose")
#> 
#> ── RMSEA power analysis ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> Test of not-close fit: H0 RMSEA ≥ .050 vs. H1 RMSEA = .010.
#> alpha = .050 · df = 100
#> 
#> Power = .870 at N = 200.

# \donttest{
# Simulation mode: hit-rate and structure recovery for a known three-factor
# population at N = 300
efa_power("simulation", Lambda = population_models$loadings$baseline,
          Phi = population_models$phis_3$moderate, N = 300,
          n_datasets = 50, criteria = c("EKC", "MAP"), seed = 42)
#> 
#> ── EFA power simulation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> 18 variables · 3 factors · N = 300 · 50 datasets
#> Estimation: PAF · rotation: oblimin
#> Model error: none (an exact population gives optimistic rates).
#> 
#> Retention hit-rate P(k-hat = 3)
#> • EKC_BvA2017: .980
#> • MAP_TR2: 1.000
#> • MAP_TR4: 1.000
#> 
#> Structure recovery (Tucker congruence ≥ .950)
#> • recovery rate (min congruence): 1.000
#> • recovery rate (mean congruence): 1.000
#> • median min congruence: .987
#> 
#> Convergence: all 50 fits converged, without Heywood cases.
#> 
#> Monte Carlo standard error of each rate: .071 or less.
# }
